message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills, modern scares, and psychological thrills—perfect for a Friday‑night binge:

| # | Title & Year | Why It Works |
|---|--------------|---------------|
| **1** | *Halloween* (1978) – John Carpenter | A timeless slasher that set the standard for jump‑scares and suspense. Great if you want pure terror without too many twists. |
| **2** | *Hereditary* (2018) – Ari Aster | Psychological dread meets supernatural horror. Its slow burn will keep you glued—and uneasy—for hours. |
| **3** | *Get Out* (2017) – Jordan Peele | Social satire + thriller. Keeps you guessing while delivering sharp social commentary. |
| **4** | *A Quiet Place* (2018) – John Krasinski | Silence as tension. Every footstep feels like an impending doom. Perfect for those who love sound design. |
| **5** | *It Follows* (2014) – David Robert Mitchell | An original take on possession/curse tropes. Creepy atmosphere plus a relentless stalker vibe. |
| **6** | *Midsommar* (2019) – Ari Aster | Daylight horror! The bright setting makes the gore even more unsettling. |
| **7** | *The Conjuring* (2013) – James Wan | Paranormal investigation meets real‑world fear. Good pacing and solid scare moments. |
| **8** | *Suspiria* (2018) – Luca Guadagnino | Visually stunning yet deeply disturbing. If you’re into art-house vibes mixed with nightmares. |
| **9** | *The Babadook* (2014) – Jennifer Kent | Horror rooted in grief and motherhood. Emotional depth adds extra layers of creepiness. |
| **10** | *Us* (2019) – Jordan Peele | Mirror image horror. Twists that stay with you long after the credits roll. |

### Quick “Watch Order” Suggestion:
1. Start with something light but still scary (*Halloween*) to get your adrenaline pumping.  
2. Move into deeper psychological territory (*Hereditary*, *Midsommar*).  
3. Finish strong with a twisty or socially relevant film (*Get Out*, *Us*).

Enjoy your fright-filled Friday night! 🎃🍿
